title: A local property of morphisms of complete weakly admissible rings stable under composition is inherited by the composite
author: The Stacks Project Authors

difficulty_reason: For a local property P of morphisms of complete weakly admissible rings which is stable under composition, and composable morphisms of locally countably indexed formal algebraic spaces, the lemma asserts that if both morphisms satisfy the equivalent conditions defining P then so does their composite (statement lines 5329-5337). The proof reduces to the affine case by three successive coverings -- of the target, then of the two base changes over each member -- and records the arrows of complete weakly admissible rings to which the members correspond (proof lines 5339-5348). The hypothesis then says that the arrows out of the base and out of the middle ring have property P at every index, so stability under composition gives that the induced arrows from the base to the sources also have P, which is exactly the condition required for the composite to satisfy P (proof lines 5348-5355). The claim is H2: the covering reduction is explicit and the only algebraic input is stability under composition, applied to the triangle of arrows read off the coverings; nothing else is assumed.
